what: The merge gate reads the pull request's published Shipping comments, not a local run artifact
why: The comment is what survives a machine restart and what a person reads; a local file only proves something happened on this disk
evidence: gate.mjs; machine/merge/gate.test.mjs refuses a stale verdict, another card's verdict and a verdict with no commit

what: A verdict only lands the commit it judged (sameCommit, at least 7 hex) and the merge uses --match-head-commit
why: Shipping reviewed a commit; a branch that moved after that review is not the change that was verified
evidence: land.mjs mergePullRequest; workflow.test.mjs "a PASS that judged an older commit does not let a moved branch land"

what: Landing facts go in docs/scorecards/<CARD>.landing.json beside the scorecard
why: scripts/scorecard.mjs regenerates <CARD>.md from Mastra's records and would overwrite an appended section; a separate file survives regeneration and puts the numbers where the scorecard is
evidence: metrics.mjs landingPath; metrics.test.mjs writes the json and leaves JUL-310.md untouched

what: Duration runs from the earliest commit on the branch (else the pull request's creation time) to the merge, and the record says which
why: The card's own work starts with its first commit; the pull request's creation is the honest fallback when the branch has one commit

what: Review rounds are the count of Shipping determinations for this card and pull request, with their verdicts in order
why: A FAIL then PASS is two rounds, and the chain is what explains the duration beside it
evidence: gate.mjs decideLanding verdicts; workflow.test.mjs expects "FAIL -> PASS"

what: The machine merges before main CI, not after
why: Branch protection is the forge's job; the machine's job is to notice when main went red on the merge commit and say so
evidence: land.mjs mergePullRequest runs plain gh pr merge; ci step polls gh run list --commit

what: Red main CI stops the run, leaves the card in progress and still runs the retro with a reflection
why: The card is not finished, but the card still failed and the lesson is worth having
evidence: workflow.mjs ci step sets failed and stop; complete step skips when stop is set and CI is not green; workflow.test.mjs covers it

what: The retro and the landing json go to main in one pull request the machine opens, checks and merges itself
why: Main is protected by a ruleset that requires the checks, so a direct push is refused outright; one pull request keeps the record and the retro it describes in the same merge, and its title names no card so the scorecard rule does not apply
evidence: land.mjs publishDocs; workflow.mjs publish step; docs/pstack-deviations.md row 14

what: The retro and the reflection are one agent step writing docs/retros/<card>.md with a ## Reflection section when the card failed
why: The repo's correct skill writes corrections and returns findings; a second agent would reread the same transcript for the same answer. The section heading is checked, so the reflection cannot be skipped silently
evidence: retro.mjs retroOutcome requires the heading when failed; retro.test.mjs covers the missing section

what: Sweep removes only this card's leftovers and keeps anything it cannot prove is idle
why: Cleanup must never take main, another card's branch, or a cost row with it
evidence: docs/scorecards/ protected; branch needs the card id and main must hold its commits; sweep.test.mjs covers each refusal

evidence: run.mjs collectLeftovers excludes the current runDir; sweep.test.mjs notices run folders that are not pr-<n>

what: The machine waits for the pull request checks before it merges

what: The merge leaves the branch to the sweep

what: The merge deletes the merged branch through the forge before main CI runs
